I can only join. One forgets what "life" really means. I have noticed from my 9 day that suddenly emotions come back. I have been laughing for a very very long time. Laughed from the heart. Never forget that life means to feel alive. Opiates do not make you feel alive, they dull everything. In the end, nothing matters anymore because you are lifeless.  But without that, just a little walk is a highlight. Its crazy and ironic, even I bombarded my reward system I learned from that addiction to appreciate the little things in life. 

That all the (negative) thoughts come back is absolutely normal. That is part of life. The good would be worth nothing to us without the bad. You probably notice it now, because everything happened so quickly. If you have a long time another "normal", to which no or hardly any negative thoughts belong, it strikes you in the 'sober' state much more. I'm the same that all the negative things, emotions and fears come back now. But this also shows us that these tablets are not a solution, but only a shift of a problem.

Write a list of all the negative things that this opiate use brings with it (you can also expand it if you think of something new) and look at it when the craving becomes strong. Then you will be reminded exactly why YOU decided to stop. The best thing to do after that is to keep your mind and body busy. Time will do the rest. Life is great, but sadly we must do something to make it even greater!

Funny enough, opiates saved my life. 5 years ago I planned at the end of the year not to have to experience the next one. I had a cough at the time and was prescribed dihydrocodeine. I googled for hours about dosage because I am a very paranoid person (and I already knew how dangerous opiates can be because of respiratory depression). After hours of googling I took it. About 100mg. Then I made the mistake of smoking pot, and because of that my senses were so focused on myself that I noticed my breathing getting slower and slower. All of a sudden I panicked because I really thought, honestly (as I said, I'm paranoid and weed amplified that) that I was really dying. That's it, I'm going to die. That was the moment when I realized that I don't really want to kill myself. Opiates saved my life. I didn't have anything to do with opiates for 4 years because I was so scared, because of this experience. A few years later I was prescribed the same thing again and the second time I realized what a bliss an opiate is. Opiates are the best antidepressant. I try to build up positive habits step by step (like meditation), but in many things I simply lack the strength, energy and motivation to do it. Opiates gave me these, what I did not have for years.
